note: Majority: Age of Majority Act, Cap. 12.02 of the Revised Laws of Saint Christopher and Nevis (2002 revision; in force 29 August 1983): a person attains full age and legal capacity at eighteen. Emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, Cap. 18.10 (in force 1 February 1939, amended to 20/2002; 2002 revision), section 2: a child is a person under sixteen and a young person one under eighteen who is no longer a child; no child may work in an industrial undertaking or on a ship (save family ones); section 7(1): no child may be employed while under twelve (save domestic and light agricultural work for parents), before the close of school hours, before six in the morning or after eight at night, for more than two hours on a school day or a Sunday, or in work injurious to health or education. So the general age is 12, with the hours limits until sixteen and sixteen for industry (my reading). Performers: section 7(4) lets a child take part without fee or reward in a charitable entertainment, lifting only the hours limits, so barred under twelve (my reading). The Act was read in the copy the University of the West Indies Cave Hill Faculty of Law Library keeps in its UNICEF Children's Law Database (a reproduction of the revised edition, held here as a secondary source because the official law site lawcommission.gov.kn refused this client (403)). Service: no defence law was read; null.

sources.title: UWI Cave Hill Law Library, UNICEF Children's Law Database: Age of Majority Act, Cap. 12.02 (Saint Christopher and Nevis, 2002 revision)
sources.said: A person shall attain full age and legal capacity on attaining the age of eighteen years.

sources.title: UWI Cave Hill Law Library, UNICEF Children's Law Database: Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, Cap. 18.10 (Saint Christopher and Nevis, 2002 revision)
sources.said: In this Act, "child" means a person under the age of sixteen years; ... so long as he or she is under twelve years ... shall prevent a child from taking part without fee or reward in an entertainment the net proceeds of which are devoted to any charitable or educational purpose
